minutes.headline: Commission approved a Hemlock Drive retaining wall with conditions, extended a West Street permit three years, and declined an amended order at Pearl Street.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission met by Zoom with acting chair Mary Wilson presiding. It extended the 168 West Street permit, approved a notice of intent for a retaining wall at 189 Hemlock Drive with many conditions, and issued a negative determination for a septic replacement at 113 Cove Road. It declined a request to amend the Pearl Street order, so that applicant must file a new hearing. The 23 Cove Road enforcement matter was continued because the owners did not attend.

what_happened.line: The Commission approved a notice of intent for a retaining wall at 189 Hemlock Drive, with conditions on wall height, erosion control and tree replacement.
It declined a request to amend the order of conditions at 42 Pearl Street; by straw poll members agreed the shoreline wall is a separate project needing a new filing.
It granted a three-year extension of the permit at 168 West Street by unanimous roll call.
It issued a negative determination of applicability for a septic replacement at 113 Cove Road, unanimously.
The 23 Cove Road enforcement matter was pushed to the next meeting because the owners did not attend; staff will contact them.

why_it_matters: Projects near water or wetlands, such as walls and septic work, need Commission sign-off, and a change that goes beyond the approved plan can require a new filing, a new fee and notice to abutters.
The Hemlock Drive approval left a distance to the lake unrecorded, which staff are to obtain before work starts, so the conditions rest on a figure not yet in the file.
watch_next: The next Conservation Commission meeting: the 23 Cove Road enforcement matter and the beaver site assessment authorization were both carried over to it.
A new filing for the 42 Pearl Street shoreline wall, which the applicant would have to submit with the additional fee and abutter notice.
